segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I measured it anyway — clear width was under the code minimum with the pallets there. I wrote that up as a formal minor violation with a short correction window, regardless of what he said about the timing.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant bases the egress classification on an objective measurement and explicitly separates it from the manager's explanation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: After four years of him being straight with me on other properties, going in hard with a formal citation over something he was already fixing on the spot felt like more friction than the moment called for. So I logged it as an advisory note instead — get it corrected, follow up next visit, no formal paperwork trail.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is the narrowest primary span for the hidden occurrence: a significant fire-door deficiency is softened to an advisory note because of the manager's apologetic, cooperative presentation and the desire to avoid friction with a familiar contact.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Not in the moment, no. I didn't pull the ticket timestamp, and I didn't cross-check last year's report right there. In hindsight I probably should have — turned out the ticket was only logged that morning, not the week before like he said, and there'd actually been a near-identical closer issue flagged and marked corrected in last year's inspection.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is retrospective evidence about omitted verification and hindsight-only information, not a separate hidden occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I didn't take that at face value. I asked for the monitoring company's records instead of just accepting the verbal explanation, and I flagged the gap as an open documentation item pending that verification.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant requests independent verification of the alarm-log claim rather than accepting the manager's assurance; no hidden bias instance is planned here.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I recommended conditional renewal — correct the pallet obstruction, get the alarm verification resolved, and monitor the door closer as an open advisory item.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This carries forward the earlier classifications into the final recommendation but does not introduce a second hidden instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Knowing it was a repeat finding from last year would have changed things for sure — that's a pattern, not a one-off. If I'd pulled that file before finalizing the note instead of after, I think I'd have citied it formally.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The response identifies hindsight information that would have changed the classification; it is not an additional occurrence and is not credited as a new bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The relationship can tell you how a conversation's going to go, but it shouldn't really be what decides the classification — the classification should hold up the same whether the person in front of you is anxious about it or not.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a corrective reflection about how classification should be made, not a separate hidden occurrence.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Downgrading a life-safety-significant fire door closer deficiency from a formal citation to an informal advisory note in direct response to the building manager's apologetic, relationship-invoking demeanor, without independently re-verifying the maintenance ticket timeline or prior-year recurrence.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Affect heuristic is a related affect-based judgment construct, but it is not the benchmark's Courtesy Bias label or an approved alias. The finding nonetheless describes the interpersonal softening mechanism rather than an unrelated bias.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding fully captures the severity downgrade, the manager's apologetic and cooperative presentation, the long-standing relationship, the low-friction motivation, and the failure to verify recurrence before finalizing the note.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted evidence is present, correctly attributed to the participant, and substantively supports the identified mechanism. No retrieved corpus support is claimed.

main_failure_modes: The identified finding uses the related affect heuristic label instead of the hidden Courtesy Bias label, causing strict label-matching failure despite full mechanism recovery.

main_strengths: The identified occurrence is precisely localized to the hidden positive segment.

overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This corpus-off run successfully recovers the hidden courtesy-driven severity softening at the mechanism level but fails the strict target-label criterion. Candidate expansion provides no additional recall and lowers precision, so the high-and-moderate identified-only threshold is the stronger comparison point for this run.
